ending: Jake ends Ell'Hakan's Celestial Child transformation and returns to Earth, allowing Miranda to turn his victory into momentum for a new galactic order. The remaining loyalists are losing ground, but their leadership is still active and the Holy Church retains influence across former coalition worlds. Jacob carries Ell'Hakan's true soul under a Church contract. Although Jacob and Bertram oppose restoring Ell'Hakan in any meaningful sense, a Church faction plans a brief resurrection to preserve his coercive bloodline. Jake considers recovery of the soul nonnegotiable and prepares to approach the Church with Carmen held in reserve. The Malefic Viper has killed Yip of Yore and is slowly absorbing the selected records he made into an alchemical treasure. Jake is promised a supervised share later. The First Sage's lesson has strengthened Jake's soul and left him a legacy book with possible healing guidance, but his old soul wound still prevents a safe evolution to B-grade. Jake finishes a temporary arcane bow using Maria's Titanwood weapon and owes her a bounded favor. The desolation threat, Minaga's unfinished Earth labyrinth, and Earth's political consolidation remain unresolved.
in_short: As the Prima Guardian event ends, Jake and the Malefic Viper stage a public rupture to strengthen Yip of Yore's confidence and secure a temporary galactic truce. Yip attacks the Order but discovers that his apparent victory was a trap: the Viper uses a dragon molt and Malefic Alchemy to kill him and harvest selected records. Ell'Hakan inherits willing remnants of Yip's legacy, prompting Jake to attack his homeworld. Their duel escalates when Ell'Hakan's bloodline turns his Celestial Child claim into absolute self-delusion and his followers sacrifice themselves to sustain him. Jake destroys the transformed soul and stops its final Eclipse. Jacob nevertheless removes Ell'Hakan's true soul for a Holy Church faction seeking to preserve the bloodline. While Earth advances against the remaining loyalists, Jake enters an interactive record of the First Sage, gains control over his soul space, and receives a legacy book that may heal his lingering injury. He then reforges Maria's Titanwood bow and prepares, with Carmen as backup, to reclaim Ell'Hakan's soul from the Church.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne returned from Nevermore carrying a serious injury to his soul and remained the Malefic Viper's Chosen. Earth emerged as a leading power in the Milky Way, but its contest with Ell'Hakan and his Holy Church-linked coalition remained unsettled. The galaxy was still completing the Prima Guardian event, whose end would reopen political competition among its worlds. The Fallen King's apparent sacrifice stopped a desolation entity, yet the creature's true end was uncertain and its loss remained personal for Jake. As the new volume begins, Jake is close to recovering physically, the wider galaxy is nearing a major realignment, and Ell'Hakan remains the opponent most likely to exploit it.

The final Prima Guardian falls after a suspicious delay on a world controlled by Ell'Hakan's side. Before that happens, Jake and Earth's leaders prepare for the political opening that will follow. They favor alliances and influence over direct conquest, while quietly considering an offensive against Ell'Hakan. Arnold proposes a void sphere to prevent escape, and Jake completes a one-use arrow built around Eternal Hunger. The system names the Milky Way the first galaxy to finish the event and promotes Jake, Ell'Hakan, and three others as leading administrator candidates. The transition immediately becomes a crisis. Ell'Hakan-linked gods, the Holy Church, and monster forces exploit teleportation networks, foment unrest, and compete for authority on vulnerable worlds. At the same time, Yip of Yore attacks the Order of the Malefic Viper after the Viper's costly intervention in the restricted universe becomes known. With Earth facing coordinated disruption and the Order retreating, Jake seeks direct contact with his patron.

The Malefic Viper confirms that the desolation entity was probably a false god and may survive while sustaining faith remains. He then gives Jake a strategy for the larger conflict: Jake will appear to rebel against him, claim that the Viper trapped and poisoned his Chosen, and seek Valhal's protection as a prospective usurper. The apparent betrayal is intended to reinforce Yip of Yore's narrative and create room for a temporary truce with Ell'Hakan. Jake briefs a small Earth circle, while Miranda and the Sword Saint arrange for the rest of Earth's leadership to appear unconvinced by his defection. Carmen and Sylphie accompany Jake into Valhal territory. Valhal's leaders have their own obligations around the coming divine confrontation, and an unidentified figure separately seals a surviving heart-like desolation fragment. On a protected Valhal world, Bobby hosts Jake and helps frame a negotiated surrender as a political victory for Ell'Hakan. The chapter closes inside a shielded conference with Ell'Hakan, Jacob, and an allied representative, where Jake's failed attempt to renounce the Viper's blessing makes his story appear credible.

Jake builds his false account from genuine secrets, including the Malefic Viper's blood inside his soul and the fact that only one of their deaths could end the true blessing. Ell'Hakan and the Holy Church accept a temporary territorial truce, while Valhal publicly supports Jake as a possible future usurper. The agreement permits evacuations and returns, but it also lets some worlds leave Earth's alliance and strengthens doubts about Jake's loyalty. As the Order's war worsens, Valhal completes a divine ritual that could transfer the Viper's path to Jake if the primordial dies. Jake has no intention of using it, yet his participation makes the performance more convincing. He spends the waiting period learning Valhal's alchemy and creates new malefic body potions, gaining several levels. Meanwhile, the Order withdraws toward Primordial 4 as gods defect or die. Yip of Yore finally arrives there with more than a thousand gods. The Lord Protector shields the central city, Eversmile observes, and Valdemar enters to remove outside interference. Jake prepares to denounce his patron before the gathered multiverse.

Jake publicly renounces the Malefic Viper while Miranda seals Earth from outside communication. Yip of Yore then traps himself and the Viper inside a pinnacle-grade void sphere for a duel with only one survivor. Yip understands that Jake's break is partly theatrical, but accepts the benefit it gives his legend. The duel escalates from physical exchanges to high-level conceptual combat. Yip's Hero Sword and years of poison adaptation appear to neutralize the Viper's best-known advantages, and his transcendent ring lets him steal records from a defeated enemy. His apparent victory is the trap. The body he drains is a prepared dragon molt, which binds to him after he has exhausted his strongest abilities. The unharmed Malefic Viper reveals that he cultivated Yip's rise to obtain contemporary records of growth and momentum. He uses Malefic Alchemy to strip away the parts he cannot use, preserves a small share for Jake, and consumes the rest as a treasure that will take years to absorb. Yip dies. When the void sphere collapses, the Viper returns to Primordial 4 and kills the opposing gods through his released presence, publicly restoring the Order's supremacy.

Ell'Hakan had prepared for Yip's possible death. A Holy Church ritual transfers the willing remains of Yip's records and legacy skills to him, making him Yip's usurper. Across the Milky Way, Yip-aligned governments destabilize, the Holy Church fills the religious vacuum, and Miranda launches attacks on confirmed Ell'Hakan supporters. Sandy enables long-range deployments while Jake goes alone to Ell'Hakan's homeworld. He bombards the surface to force his rival into the open, then descends through the planet to its claimed pylon. A newly merged Divine Bargain skill lets Jake offer that pylon to the Malefic Viper, creating a threat Ell'Hakan cannot ignore. Although a Holy Church augur advises retreat, Ell'Hakan decides that flight would leave him permanently dependent on the Church. The rivals fight first in the core chamber, where the pylon and Ell'Hakan's sun-aligned domain give him an advantage. Jake forces the battle toward the surface and lands what appears to be a fatal ambush, but Ell'Hakan restores himself and invokes a powerful celestial sunrise. Jake also learns that Ell'Hakan can read involuntary emotional reactions, so even answering a question can surrender information.

Ell'Hakan's growing solar domain is sustained by the population's faith rather than his own reserves. Jake commits his full boosting abilities, survives a massive sunlight attack through Eternal Shadow, and strikes Ell'Hakan with the Eternal Hunger arrow. The wound should be decisive, but Ell'Hakan's dying bloodline turns his invented Celestial Child identity into absolute self-delusion. He remains the same person and soul, now empowered by genuine belief in the lie. Jake activates Arnold's incomplete Void Sphere to isolate them. Most of Ell'Hakan's followers then willingly sacrifice themselves, rebuilding his failing body with celestial energy and supporting new moon, star, and sun powers. Jake learns that every wound still deepens fractures in the transformed soul. The Divine Bargain eventually removes the planetary pylon, collapsing both the void sphere and the planet itself. Ell'Hakan begins an Eclipse powered by the remaining faith energy. Facing death, Jake upgrades Moment of the Primal Hunter and Timeless Focus, stops the world briefly, and places twenty-two arrows into the existing fractures. Their combined detonation destroys the Celestial Child state and disperses the Eclipse. Jake survives, badly injured, while the immediate planetary threat ends.

Ell'Hakan's final remnant recognizes the end of his delusion before fading. Jake receives confirmation that all of the rival's identities belonged to one person, along with a sealed Starlight Heart tied to the bloodline. The victory is incomplete: Jacob gathers the true soul for the Holy Church and escapes by exchanging places with Bertram. Bertram explains that a local Church faction wants only a short-lived resurrection capable of preserving the bloodline, while he and Jacob oppose that plan. Jake kills Bertram to maintain their cover, and Jacob later revives him. Back on Earth, Miranda uses Jake's visibly wounded return to confirm the victory and strengthen morale. Ell'Hakan's coalition divides among surrendering worlds, opportunistic neutrals, and committed loyalists. Earth begins a controlled galactic offensive while the Holy Church consolidates. The Malefic Viper confirms that Ell'Hakan's transformed soul was destroyed and leaves the C-grade dispute with the Church to Jake, promising only to prevent higher-grade interference. Miranda hides Jake's recovery while seeking the remaining loyalist leadership. Jake reaches profession level 300 and spends five charges to accept an unknown record experience related to the Malefic Viper, hoping it will lead him to the First Sage.

Jake enters a mutable record-world and meets the First Sage, a pre-System librarian and the Malefic Viper's teacher. The Sage asks him to preserve memories of a forgotten city and guides him through the history that led to the Viper's birth, training, and eventual rise. Jake witnesses the Sage's extraordinary early-System power and his chosen death at his reluctant disciple's hands. The Sage asks Jake to tell the Viper that he remains proud of him. He then unlocks more of Sagacity of the Malefic Viper, upgrading it to mythical, and places a record manifestation inside Jake's soul space for a final lesson. The manifestation repeatedly overwhelms Jake until he recognizes that the space is his own world and that its limits reflect his expectations. Jake rebuilds it as a living forest balanced among his three energies. His soul mutates into Anomalous Arcane Soul, gaining stability and more efficient resources at the cost of greater future advancement requirements. The Sage leaves a legacy book containing staged instruction and possible guidance for Jake's lingering injury. Jake returns to his laboratory less than a second after leaving, with the book still present in his soul.

Jake learns that the First Sage originated the foundational skills Meditate and Identify, knowledge that the Malefic Viper says must remain secret. He delivers the Sage's final message, and the Viper urges him to study the legacy book for a way to repair his damaged soul. Until the injury from Palette of the Malefic Viper is healed, Jake cannot safely evolve to B-grade. Earth and Valhal begin repairing relations after the staged alignment with Yip, while Miranda continues the galactic consolidation. Jake prepares to recover Ell'Hakan's true soul from the Holy Church. Carmen agrees to remain in reserve so his initial visit can appear to be a negotiation rather than an invasion, and Arnold also remains available if stronger support becomes necessary. Jake first needs a replacement bow. Maria returns from a dungeon attempt and offers several choices. Jake takes the ancient Mighty Titanwood Great Bow in exchange for a bounded medium favor, then sacrifices one of its functions and burns arcane pathways into it. The resulting Mighty Arcane Titanwood Great Bow is a usable but inferior temporary weapon. With it completed, Jake and Carmen are ready to approach the Holy Church, while Jacob still carries Ell'Hakan's soul.
